rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes substrate pre-heating during SLM, whereas the paper used atmosphere-controlled debinding of DLP-printed green bodies. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (additive manufacturing process modification vs. post-printing thermal treatment atmosphere control).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies SLM processing conditions (laser power, scan strategies, inert atmosphere) for CoCrFeNiMn, while the paper used DLP printing, debinding with specific holds, and sintering at 800–1100 °C for AlCrFeNiSi. There is no overlap in processing regime or conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes reduced thermal gradients and residual stress mitigation, while the paper's mechanism involves carbon retention, reduced gas evolution, and oxide-layer effects on densification. These are entirely different mechanistic classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved dimensional fidelity and mechanical properties (yield strength, ductility) for SLM parts, whereas the paper reports earlier densification and comparable compressive strength at a lower sintering temperature. The predicted properties and direction of improvement are unrelated.
